QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_12

question.text: Under Regulation 27 of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, how long after the winding up of an AIF must the Manager/Sponsor retain records such as valuation policies, investment strategies, investor particulars and contribution, and investment rationale?

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 27 requires records of (a) assets under the fund/scheme, (b) valuation policies and practices, (c) investment strategies, (d) particulars of investors and contribution, and (e) rationale for investments — to be maintained for 5 years AFTER the winding up of the fund. The Trap: 3 years is the common Income-tax retention period (but extended for scrutiny). 8 years is the PMLA record retention norm (cross-cat, for onboarding docs). 10 years is a common ERISA/US norm, not Indian AIF. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV (AML) drills 5-year PMLA retention for KYC/CDD separately. Do not confuse Reg 27 (post-winding-up) with PMLA (ongoing from transaction date). Manager's Pro-Tip: Cloud-archive all valuation committee minutes, IC memos, and investor wire instructions in a dedicated S3 bucket with 5-year lifecycle policy. SEBI inspections post-winding-up DO happen, and absence of records is an independent compliance failure.
